name: Kojiya
tagline: Shinagawa in 25 minutes and Tokyo in 39 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Ota City, served by Keikyu Airport Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 46 minutes to Otemachi, 56 minutes to Shinjuku, 51 minutes to Shibuya and 25 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 2.2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 2.2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.7 m to 2.6 m, a difference of 0.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: マルエツ 糀谷駅南口店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 9 clinics and 6 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 有仁会糀谷病院, about 2 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 幸和病院, about 10 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Keikyu Airport Line.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Keikyu Airport Line. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Keikyu-Kamata is ahead on the number of lines and how close the centre is, but Kojiya is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Kojiya. Keikyu-Kamata also has the Keikyu Main Line, which Kojiya does not. With more lines, Keikyu-Kamata is the better connected of the two. To Otemachi, for instance, Keikyu-Kamata is 8 minutes quicker. On what it offers families, though, Kojiya comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Kojiya is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Kojiya. It is served by the same lines as Kojiya. To Tokyo, for instance, Otorii takes 3 minutes longer. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 7 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Keikyu Airport Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
